REQUEST

The Applicant is proposing to legalize an existing block retaining wall with attached tubular
fencing that is an overall height of 12 feet. In addition, the Applicant is also proposing to
legalize an existing 546 SF playroom with an attached 327 SF screened patio. Modification
No. 10-20 is requested to allow the maximum fence/wall height to deviate from six (6) feet to
twelve (12) feet. Modification No. 04-21 is requested to allow the required side setback of
the playroom/patio to deviate from 4’-0” to 2’-2”. The subject site is located in the R-1C
(Single Family Residential) zone in the Rurban Homestead Overlay District (RHOD). The
Modification request is made pursuant to Chapter 17.20 (Modification–Variance) of the El
Monte Municipal Code (EMMC).

DISCUSSION

The property is currently improved with a two-story 2,240 SF single-family dwelling with an
attached 576 SF garage and an attached 240 SF carport. The existing single-family
residence contains four (4) bedroom and three (3) bathrooms and was constructed in 1949.
Building and Safety records reflect that a permit was issued for the construction of a
detached playroom in 1992. Records also reflect that the permit for the playroom was
canceled in 1993. Based on this information, the previously issued permit is rendered null
and void. It should be noted that the permit that was previously issued for the playroom did
not include plumbing. The proposed legalization of the existing playroom includes the
request to legalize a 36 SF bathroom within the playroom. The applicant is also proposing to
legalize a 327 SF screened patio that is attached to the playroom. A request to deviate from
the side setback from 4’-0” to 2’-2” is included with the proposed legalization of the playroom
and attached patio.

Additionally, the applicant is proposing to legalize an existing retaining wall that is located
along the easterly property line that is an overall height of 12 feet and 40 feet in length. The
existing zoning allows a maximum height of 6’-0” for a wall/fence that is located behind the
front setback area in residential zones. The existing wall proposed to be legalized is located
behind the front setback area and is not visible from the street. A Modification request to
deviate from a height of 6’-0” to 12’-0” is included with the proposed legalization of the
retaining wall with attached tubular fencing.

FINDINGS OF FACT

In order to approve the project, the Modification Committee is required to make certain
findings. Section 17.20.020 (EMMC) - Necessary conditions outlines the four (4) required
findings and conditions to be met in order to approve any Modification:

FINDING:

  A. There are exceptional or extraordinary circumstances or conditions applicable to the
  property involved, or to the intended use of the property, that do not apply generally to
  the property or class of use in the same zone or vicinity;

FACT:

  According to Building and Safety records, a permit was issued in 1992 for a playroom
  excluding plumbing. Records also reflect that the permit for the playroom was

  12125 Hemlock Street
  MOD Nos. 10-20 and 04-21
   canceled in 1993. Based on this information, the previously issued building permit is
  rendered null and void. Due to the fact that the existing playroom was constructed
  under a valid building permit, the circumstances may be considered exceptional or
  unique because the playroom structure was constructed under a valid permit,
  however it was not finalized. Building and Safety records reflect that the side setback
  proposed for the detached playroom is approximately ±2’-0” on the approved set of
  plans. The applicant is seeking to legalize what was previously was approved. Per
  Section 17.06.070(E) of the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC) accessory structures
  shall have a minimum setback of 4’-0”. Granting the deviation from the required
  setback from 4’-0” to 2’-2” will allow the property owner to bring the existing structure
  into conformance.

  The proposed legalization of the retaining wall is considered an extraordinary
  circumstance due to the significant difference in grade of the subject site in
  comparison to the site located to the east. The applicant is conditioned to obtain the
  required notarized neighbor awareness form for the proposed property line wall.

FINDING:

  B. The granting of such variance will not be materially detrimental to the public health or
  welfare or injurious to the property or improvements in such zone or vicinity in which
  the property is located;

FACT:

  Granting the Modification will not be detrimental to the public health or welfare or
  injurious to the properties in the vicinity for the proposed legalization of the playroom
  with an attached patio as it would allow the property owner to bring the existing
  structure into conformance by the granting of the requested side setback deviation to
  meet existing zoning code requirements. The proposed legalization of the playroom
  with an attached patio and 36 SF bathroom is conditioned to meet all Building and
  Safety requirements which would ensure that the proposed is not detrimental to public
  health and safety.

  Granting the Modification will not be detrimental to the public health or welfare or
  injurious to the properties in the vicinity for the proposed legalization of the existing
  retaining wall with an overall height of 12 feet. The project is conditioned to meet all
  Building and Safety requirements, including but not limited to providing a structural
  engineer report with the level of detail to the satisfaction of the Building and Safety
  Division. These requirements will be verified during the plan check phase. Meeting
  all Building and Safety requirements will ensure that the proposed is not detrimental to
  public health and safety.

  There will be no impacts to nearby properties such as daylight obstruction, visual
  blight, etc. The location of the playroom and retaining wall are not visible from the
  street thus minimizing the impact to surrounding properties. Moreover the property will
  remain under the maximum Floor Area Ratio (FAR) and lot coverage.
  12125 Hemlock Street
  MOD Nos. 10-20 and 04-21
 FINDING:

  C. Because of special circumstances applicable to subject property, including size,
  shape, topography, location or surroundings, the strict application of the zoning
  ordinance is found to deprive subject property of privileges enjoyed by other
  properties in the vicinity and under the identical zone classifications;

FACT:

  Staff has determined that the requested modification for the deviation of the side
  setback for the legalization of the detached playroom and attached patio can be
  supported due to the fact that the existing playroom structure side setback is
  consistent with the plans that were previously approved in 1992. At the time, the
  playroom was constructed under a valid building permit, however the permit was later
  canceled in 1993. The cancellation of the building permit has rendered the permit null
  and void. The granting of the deviation of the side setback would allow the property
  owner to bring the structure with the attached patio into conformance as the existing
  zoning code requires accessory structures to have a minimum 4’-0” side setback.

  Staff has also determined that the requested modification to deviate from the
  maximum wall height can be supported due to the significant difference in grade in
  comparison with the adjacent property to the east.

FINDING:

  D. The granting of such variance will not adversely affect the comprehensive general
  plan.

FACT:

  The approval of such modification to reduce the required accessory structure side
  setback from 4’-0” to 2’-2” will not adversely affect the comprehensive General Plan.
  Policy LU-1.1-Code Compliance, ensures land compatibility through adherence to the
  policies, standards, and regulations in the Municipal Code; Policy LU-1.6-Quality of
  Life, encourages protecting the quality of life of residents. Allowing the deviation of the
  accessory structure side setback will allow the property owner to retain the existing
  playroom structure thus enhancing the livability of the property while maintaining the
  single family residence characteristic of the Low Density Residential designation.
  Additionally, it is found that the proposed deviation from the maximum wall height from
  6’-0” to 12’-0” in combination with meeting all Building and Safety requirements is also
  compatible with the intent of the General Plan as it will grant the property owner a
  solution to addressing the significant difference in grade in comparison to the adjacent
  property to the east.

  12125 Hemlock Street
  MOD Nos. 10-20 and 04-21
 CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL:

  1. The project shall substantially conform to the site plan, floor plan and elevation
  plans on file with the City’s Planning Division and as presented to the Modification
  Committee on June 8, 2021 and as amended herein.

  2. Plans shall comply with all City Department/Divisions regulations, guidelines, and
  conditions of approval including Building, Engineering, Planning and the Los
  Angeles County Fire Department.

  3. The project shall conform to the 2019 California Building Codes including but not
  limited to the California Green Building Code.

  4. A Structural Engineer Report shall be submitted upon initiating the plan check
  phase including the level of detail to the satisfaction of the Building and Safety
  Division. The project shall conform and adhere to all Building and Safety
  requirements.

  5. A notarized Neighbor Awareness Form is required and shall be submitted upon
  initiating the plan check phase for the proposed legalization of the property line
  wall/fence.

  6. The approval of Modification Nos. 10-20 and 04-21 is valid for one (1) year from
  the date of approval. During this time period, the applicant is responsible for
  obtaining the required City permit(s) for the proposed project.

  7. The bathroom located within the playroom shall comply with all requirements
  specified in Section 17.06.070(F) of the El Monte Municipal Code (EMMC),
  including but not limited to a covenant that is signed and recorded against the
  property stating that the structure in which the bathroom is located will not be
  converted to an accessory dwelling unit or a sleeping/living quarter without
  obtaining the necessary permits from the City.

  8. A copy of the final decision letter with the conditions of approval shall be submitted
  with the building plans.

  9. The playroom and attached patio shall be finished with building/finish materials
  that complement and match the existing residence.

  12125 Hemlock Street
  MOD Nos. 10-20 and 04-21
 RECOMMENDATION:

Staff recommends that the Modification Committee evaluate the proposal and consider the
following Action:

  1. Adopt a Categorical Exemption under Section 15303 (Class 3–New Construction or
  Conversion of Small Structures) pursuant to the California Environmental Quality Act
  and Guidelines, as amended and;

  2. Adopt the finding of Facts to approve Modification Nos. 10-20 and 04-21, subject to
  the conditions of approval.
